# ADR-060 — A 202 on a confirm means a commit will be ATTEMPTED; every Android capture launch is consumed exactly once (Checkpoint 8.4)

**Status:** Locked

<!-- Decision text below is verbatim from the pre-split docs/DECISIONS.md table row (2026-09-16). Do not edit a Locked decision without explicit owner approval. -->

**A 202 on a confirm means a commit will be ATTEMPTED, and every Android capture launch is consumed exactly once (Checkpoint 8.4, 2026-09-03).** Two contracts, both written down because the first was already violated in production and the second is the only thing standing between one gesture and two Inbox rows. **1. THE CONFIRM CONTRACT.** `unclear` is a legitimate parser outcome — one of the four tools the model may call — but it has no entity to create, and `commitParsedEntity` has always ended `case "unclear": throw`. Nothing consulted that before enqueueing, so `POST /inbox/:id/confirm` returned **202 for work that could only ever fail**, the job burned all five retries, and the item was left exactly as it was with the user told nothing. Verified first-hand against production: two items, both storing `unclear`, both jobs `retry_count 5/5`, `job.output` reading only `AiJobError: capture.parse failed (Error)`, and **three worker log lines in the entire 40-minute window, none of them about the failures**. The contract is now: **the API computes the EFFECTIVE tool call — the caller's correction if supplied, otherwise the stored one — and refuses an uncommittable confirm with `409 parse_result_not_committable` BEFORE enqueueing anything.** The refusal echoes the tool **enum only**; the `unclear` tool's own `reason` argument is derived from capture text and is deliberately never returned. Three further defects on the same path are closed with it, each silent on its own: `corrected_tool_call` was `z.unknown()` so a correction was never validated; the API stored a correction as a **bare tool call** while the worker reads `parse_result.toolCall`, which made the documented escape hatch from an unclear parse **itself broken**; and the mobile mutation had **no error path at all**, so 404, 409 and 503 were indistinguishable from success. The worker keeps a defence-in-depth guard that treats an uncommittable or unreadable confirm as **permanent rather than retryable** — retrying recomputes the same answer — and every `capture.parse` failure is now classified by **stage** (`load_row` / `confirm_commit` / `auto_parse` / `confirmation_push`) through `errorToken`, which by construction can carry neither provider prose nor capture text. **`AiJobError`'s containment is unchanged and remains correct**; what was missing was any classification beside it, which is why a provider outage, a Postgres error and a commit-invariant violation all persisted as one identical string. **`capture.parse` still has no dead-letter queue** — it remains the only retrying queue without one — and that is recorded as debt rather than fixed here. **2. THE CAPTURE-INTENT CONTRACT.** The Android share sheet and the launcher shortcut both mean "the owner wants to capture something", so both go through one local Expo module and one composer rather than two mechanisms; `source: "share"` and its CHECK value already existed, so **no migration**. Four rules, each closing a specific way one gesture becomes two rows: the launch intent is **sticky** and Android re-delivers it after process death plus restore from Recents, so the native side **consumes and neuters** it rather than exposing a getter; the warm path reads the Intent handed to `OnNewIntent` and **never `activity.intent`**, because React Native's `ReactActivity.onNewIntent` never calls `setIntent()` and that field therefore keeps returning the original launch intent for the Activity's whole life; the **native intent id becomes the capture's `client_uuid`**, which turns the server's existing dedupe into a real backstop rather than decoration (a fresh `randomUUID()` per submit defeats it entirely); and the claimed-id set lives at **module scope**, because the hazard being defended against is precisely a remount. A share **pre-fills the composer instead of submitting**: the text came from another app, the owner sees exactly what will be captured, and nothing is posted without a tap. Shared text is control-character-stripped **before** truncation (the Checkpoint 8.1 ordering, so invisible codepoints cannot consume the length budget) and bounded by the same constant the server enforces. **Nothing interprets it** — no HTML, no Markdown, no autolink, and no route is ever derived from capture text. **3. NOTIFICATION-SHADE CAPTURE IS DEFERRED ON EVIDENCE, NOT ATTEMPTED AND ABANDONED.** Android direct reply IS natively implemented in the installed `expo-notifications@57.0.12`. It is nonetheless not viable: with the app process dead — the normal state for a shade affordance — the reply is parked in a static in-process collection and lost if the process dies before JS boots, and the durable path requires **`expo-task-manager`, verified absent** from the dependency set. Shipping it would silently lose captures, which is the one failure `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`'s persist-before-send design exists to prevent. **Neither contract required a migration** — level stays 16 (Checkpoint 8.4, 2026-09-03) **[Present state corrected by ADR-061.]**
